disclaimer: Step-by-step guidance is informational only. Always verify the current process at VA.gov before submitting forms.

benefits.title: VA Disability Compensation
benefits.summary: Tax-free monthly payment for service-connected conditions. The earlier you file, the earlier your effective date and back pay.
benefits.eligibilityNotes: Active-duty, Guard, or Reserve service with a current condition linked to that service. Discharge other than dishonorable. Even 0% rated claims are worth filing — they unlock other benefits.

steps.title: Gather your evidence
steps.description: Pull your DD-214, Service Treatment Records, and any current diagnosis paperwork. A nexus letter from your doctor is the single most useful document.

steps.title: Submit an Intent to File (Form 21-0966)
steps.description: This locks in your effective date for back pay while you finish the rest of the claim. Takes ~5 minutes.

steps.title: File the claim on VA.gov or with a VSO
steps.description: File online at VA.gov, or work with a free Veterans Service Officer (DAV, VFW, American Legion). VSOs are free and dramatically improve approval odds.

steps.title: Attend C&P exams
steps.description: VA will schedule Compensation & Pension exams. Show up, be honest about your worst day (not your best), and describe how the condition affects daily life.

steps.title: Track and appeal
steps.description: Decisions land on VA.gov in 3–6 months. If a rating is low, you can file a Higher-Level Review or Supplemental Claim within a year.

benefits.title: Post-9/11 GI Bill
benefits.summary: Up to 36 months of tuition, a monthly housing stipend, and a books allowance. Use it for college, trade school, certifications, or apprenticeships.
benefits.eligibilityNotes: At least 90 days of active duty after Sep 10, 2001 (or 30 days with a service-connected discharge). Forever GI Bill removes the 15-year expiration for service that ended on or after Jan 1, 2013.

steps.title: Apply for your Certificate of Eligibility
steps.description: Submit VA Form 22-1990 on VA.gov. The Certificate of Eligibility (COE) tells you and your school how many months you have left.

steps.title: Pick an approved school or program
steps.description: Use the GI Bill Comparison Tool to check tuition cap, BAH rate, graduation outcomes, and complaints history.

steps.title: Enroll and submit a VA-22-1995 if you transfer
steps.description: Talk to your school's VA certifying official. They submit your enrollment to VA each term.

steps.title: Verify enrollment monthly
steps.description: Use Enrollment Verification on VA.gov or text VETTEXT to keep your housing payments flowing.

benefits.title: VA Home Loan
benefits.summary: Zero down payment, no PMI, and competitive rates — the most valuable financial benefit most veterans never use.
benefits.eligibilityNotes: 90+ days of active service during wartime, 181+ days during peacetime, or 6 years in the National Guard / Reserve. Surviving spouses can also qualify.

steps.title: Request your Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
steps.description: Apply on VA.gov in ~5 minutes, or have a VA-approved lender pull it for you instantly.

steps.title: Shop multiple VA-approved lenders
steps.description: Get Loan Estimates from at least 3 lenders. The funding fee is lender-neutral; rates and origination fees are not.

steps.title: Get pre-approved
steps.description: A pre-approval letter shows sellers you are serious and locks in the property limits you can afford.

steps.title: Find the home and get a VA appraisal
steps.description: VA appraisers check fair value AND minimum property requirements. Plan for 2–3 weeks.

steps.title: Close — and ask about the funding fee waiver
steps.description: Veterans receiving disability compensation are exempt from the funding fee. Make your lender confirm this in writing before closing.

benefits.title: Veteran Readiness & Employment (VR&E)
benefits.summary: Career counseling, training, and tuition (often more generous than the GI Bill) for veterans with a service-connected disability.
benefits.eligibilityNotes: Service-connected disability rating of 10% or higher (in some cases 20%) and an employment handicap. Eligibility window has been removed for many discharges.

steps.title: Apply with VA Form 28-1900
steps.description: Submit on VA.gov. You will be contacted to schedule an Initial Counseling appointment with a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor (VRC).

steps.title: Attend your Initial Counseling
steps.description: The VRC builds a Rehabilitation Plan with you — could be Reemployment, Rapid Access to Employment, Self-Employment, Employment Through Long-Term Services, or Independent Living.

steps.title: Sign your Plan and receive subsistence allowance
steps.description: Once approved, your tuition and fees are paid directly and you receive a monthly subsistence allowance while in the program.

benefits.title: Tricare Health Coverage
benefits.summary: Health coverage for retirees, medically retired veterans, and their families. Most newly separated veterans should also enroll in VA Health Care.
benefits.eligibilityNotes: Active-duty retirees and medical retirees qualify for Tricare. All other recently separated veterans should enroll in VA Health Care via Form 10-10EZ — combat veterans get 10 years of enhanced eligibility.

steps.title: Decide: Tricare or VA Health Care (or both)
steps.description: Retirees default to Tricare; non-retirees enroll in VA Health Care. Many veterans are eligible for both and use VA primary care + Tricare for family.

steps.title: Apply for VA Health Care (Form 10-10EZ)
steps.description: Apply on VA.gov in ~10 minutes. Combat veterans separated after 1998 receive 10 years of enhanced enrollment regardless of priority group.

steps.title: Enroll in Tricare (retirees) within 90 days
steps.description: Update DEERS first, then choose Tricare Prime, Select, or For Life depending on age and Medicare status.
